newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares up in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares up in quiet trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices rose on Wednesday in quiet trade.
The Capital Market Authority index added 1.62 points to end at 335.15 in 41.7 million pounds ($12.3 million) worth of trade.
"I cannot call it a reversal...but the market has bottomed out and it is bullish now," said Bassim Arida, analyst at Prime Investments.
National Societe Generale Bank was among the busiest shares on the day, climbing 3.08 pounds to close at 73.8, when equity worth 2.27 million pounds were traded.
"Societe Generale is among the top five banks in Egypt. It has a P/E of 13, which is very good for banking," said Arida. "The price is so attractive that it says 'please take me up'."
The blue-chip of banks, Commercial International Bank/CIB, was active as usual. The share shed 0.37 pounds to 73.65, after trading in shares worth 3.2 million pounds.
Amriyah Cement closed 0.14 pounds up at 79.94 in a mediocre 812,028 pounds trade.

The equity was not affected by the government's announced plan to sell its full stake of 48 percent in the firm through the bourse and via a Global Depository Receipts (GDR). No date was set for the sale.
"Amriyah has a P/E of 10, which is low. The fact that the government will be fully out (of the firm) is a healthy sign," Arida said.

Shawkat Raslan, a broker at Prime, said the share had not been affected by the announcement because mutual funds held large amounts of the equity and were interested in preserving the stability of its price.
Medinet Nasr Housing and Development slipped again 0.8 pounds to 237.9. Shares worth 2.87 million changed hands.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 451.91 points from 449.54 points on Tuesday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 249.78 to 248.63.
Of the 95 shares traded, 55 rose, 30 ended lower and 10 remained unchanged.
